title: PowerPoint on desktop: reference a PowerPoint file when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, Reference file workflow, licence requirement and both control routes are supported. One Microsoft readiness guide uses a different label for the SharePoint discovery setting; the briefing should acknowledge that documentation difference.

claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint can reference the content of an existing PowerPoint file when creating a presentation.
claims.quote: You can now reference the content of a PowerPoint file when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: title; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The roadmap calls this capability Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Reference the content of a PowerPoint file when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Copilot features roll out gradually to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organisation.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a default specifically for Reference file, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Reference file default admin switch; PowerPoint Reference file default policy; Copilot PowerPoint reference existing presentations admin controls rollout default. Opened release notes, Copilot overview, privacy and admin settings pages; no feature-specific default stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no switch specific to Reference file.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Reference file default admin switch; PowerPoint Reference file default policy; Copilot PowerPoint reference existing presentations admin controls rollout default. Opened release notes, privacy and Copilot admin settings; found broader controls, no Reference file switch.

claims.claim: Connected-experience privacy controls can disable Copilot in PowerPoint on current Windows and Mac apps.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps: ... PowerPoint ... most current version ... Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.claim: The feature's release note describes user steps and no admin enablement step.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference existing presentations admin controls rollout default. Read the complete July 01 Reference file entry in release notes: Open PowerPoint, start edit with Copilot, select Reference file, ask Copilot; no admin enablement step.

claims.claim: The release-note workflow adds no new sign-in or consent step.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference existing presentations admin controls rollout default. Read the complete July 01 Reference file release-note entry, including permissions and both Try this workflows; neither lists a new sign-in or consent step.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Reference file uses the Premium edit-with-Copilot experience requiring a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence; it is included in that product licence.
claims.quote: Edit with Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote ... ^2^ Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) features: A Microsoft 365 Copilot license is required to access this feature.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat (Basic) users do not have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license and don't have access to Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat (Basic) users lack access to Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license and don't have access to Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users do not have the Copilot add-on licence.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The Basic tier's listed PowerPoint features include creating presentations from prompts.
claims.quote: PowerPoint: Create presentations from prompts or existing content, summarize presentations or edit presentations (add images, apply deck-wide formatting changes)

claims.claim: The Basic tier's listed PowerPoint features include creating presentations from existing content.
claims.quote: PowerPoint: Create presentations from prompts or existing content, summarize presentations or edit presentations (add images, apply deck-wide formatting changes)

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) users have the add-on licence.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Premium provides the full Copilot experience in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The overview says some features are subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.claim: Whether a fair use limit applies specifically to Reference file is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Reference file fair use limits pricing meter; Copilot PowerPoint reference presentation fair use limits licensing pricing. Opened overview, service description, release notes and Limits for features in Microsoft Copilot Chat; none specifies a Reference file fair use limit.

claims.claim: Learn publishes no separate meter for Reference file at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Reference file fair use limits pricing meter; Copilot PowerPoint reference presentation fair use limits licensing pricing. Opened Copilot overview, service description and release notes; no separate Reference file meter documented.

claims.claim: Learn publishes no separate price for Reference file at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Reference file fair use limits pricing meter; Copilot PowerPoint reference presentation fair use limits licensing pricing. Opened overview, service description and release notes; licensing search also returned License options for Microsoft Copilot, no separate feature price.

claims.claim: The release-note entry names no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference presentation fair use limits licensing pricing. Read the complete July 01 Reference file entry in release notes: description, What changed, permissions, Why and both Try this workflows; no licence named in the entry.

claims.claim: Licences are assigned in Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user ... In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PowerShell assigns the user's licence with Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @().
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The licence row manages product entitlement rather than a Reference file-specific setting or file permissions.
claims.quote: When you use the Active users page to assign or unassign licenses, you assign or unassign users licenses to products.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is configured in SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.
claims.fix: Keep the cited path. Add to the control note: 'Microsoft's readiness guide alternatively labels the setting Restrict content discovery > On.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/get-ready-copilot-sharepoint-advanced-management#step-3-prevent-accidental-oversharing, which says 'Under Restrict content discovery, select On.'

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is enabled with Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true.
claims.quote: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits discovery of content from selected SharePoint sites in Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes discoverability, not existing file permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery can be applied only to SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is not supported for OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect experiences operating on content already in use by the user.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.

claims.claim: Learn does not specify whether Restricted Content Discovery stops a file explicitly selected with Reference file.
claims.quote: Searched: Reference file Restricted Content Discovery. Read Restricted Content Discovery and Reference file release notes; search returned SharePoint readiness and prompt-defense excerpts. Discovery is covered and already-in-use content exempted, but explicit Reference file selection is not specified.

claims.claim: The Copilot settings page groups settings under User access, Data access, Copilot actions and Other settings.
claims.quote: Browse User access, Data access, Copilot actions, and Other settings. Select View all or All settings when a setting isn't shown in a category.

claims.claim: The Copilot admin settings article lists no setting named for Copilot in PowerPoint or Reference file.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Reference file default admin switch; Copilot PowerPoint reference existing presentations admin controls rollout default. Read the full Configure Microsoft Copilot settings article, all four categories and app-experience controls; neither setting name appears.
